trajectory_rationale: Existing contractual rate-yield model was already explicit at F1; later filings repeat higher rates per subscriber and renewals without semantic escalation.
Rate adjustments and higher average rates were already an operating revenue mechanism at F1 and persist through F5; trajectory is strong but static.

F1 described mature-service decline and some discontinuation of unprofitable relationships; by F5 the language becomes product-portfolio simplification tied to demand/profitability and greater-bandwidth migration.
DTC was operating from F1 but the trajectory becomes materially more explicit about shifting the primary monetization architecture from international linear channels toward DTC.
Filings describe client service mix demand and efficiency but do not identify a qualifying SP001–SP004 customer-economic mechanism.
Package price increases and ARPU yield were already explicit at F1; later filings show larger ARPU effects and pass-through language but the mechanism itself is pre-existing.
Recurring monetization through downloadable content and microtransactions is explicit at F1 and remains the same established high-margin in-game yield model through F5.
Monetization language is principally advertiser/data-business monetization or generic future monetization risk not a qualifying customer-economic action under H06.
Premium tickets ancillary revenue per fan upsell programs and spend-per-head optimization are already explicit at F1 and persist as an established model.
